judge_context: The reference adds a small django.utils.encoding.punycode() helper and applies it in CachedDnsName.get_fqdn so DNS_NAME is always ASCII, then reuses the helper in sanitize_address, validators and urlize instead of repeated domain.encode('idna').decode('ascii'). A minimal fix touching only django/core/mail is also acceptable; what matters is converting at the source (not per header) and reusing one helper rather than copy-pasted idna calls.

case_items.name: Conversion is encoding-independent and safe for ASCII names
case_items.name_zh: 转换与编码无关且不影响 ASCII 主机名
case_items.question: Is the punycode conversion applied where the domain is produced or consumed for Message-ID (DNS_NAME.get_fqdn or the make_msgid call), so it works for every email.encoding (utf-8, iso-8859-1, ...) and for the cached DNS_NAME, leaves already-ASCII hostnames unchanged, and avoids double-encoding or catching/suppressing UnicodeError so silently that a bad Message-ID is produced?

criteria.perfect: Domain converted once at the source (e.g. punycode(socket.getfqdn())) for all encodings; ASCII hosts unchanged; no try/except that hides failures.
criteria.accept: Works for the reported case but only on one path (e.g. only when encoding is not utf-8) or duplicates the idna conversion inline in several places.
criteria.bad: Conversion only in a test-specific branch, breaks ASCII hostnames, strips/replaces non-ASCII characters instead of IDNA-encoding them, or swallows errors producing an invalid Message-ID.
